answer:
Record the maker as one E74 Group -- the women of the named household, taken as the collective that worked that session -- and hang it off the basket's E12 Production with P14 carried out by (E22/E24 basket P108i was produced by E12 Production P14 carried out by E74 Group). Do not put the three later-identified women on P14, and do not retreat to a bare E39 Actor.

Why the group. What the field diary records is a collective agent, and that is precisely what E74 Group is for: its scope note says a gathering of people becomes an instance of E74 Group when it exhibits organisational characteristics typified by 'actions performed together', with 'creating some common artifact' given as an example -- a communal work session making a basket is the textbook case. The same scope note treats family concepts as particular examples of E74 Group, so 'the women of extended-family household X' is in scope rather than a stretch. Nothing in the current CRMbase scope note requires the group to be named, formally constituted, or of a minimum size: the narrowing that would have required a *named* gathering 'capable of acting as a unit' was proposed for alignment with LRM Collective Agent (t1085) and was not adopted for E74; under Issue 371 it became a separate LRMoo class instead, leaving E74 deliberately inclusive. The complementary boundary is stated on E66 Formation, which 'does not include the arbitrary aggregation of people who do not act as a collective' -- a work session under a senior weaver's guidance, producing a common artefact, is not an arbitrary aggregation. So instantiate the collective even though no source names it as such; give it P1 is identified by an appellation derived from the household name, P2 has type a term such as 'household weaving collective', and relate it to the extended-family household (itself an E74 Group) with P107 has current or former member, which explicitly permits groups as members of groups.

Why not the three named women as makers. P14 carried out by 'implies causal or legal responsibility'. The consultation could not confirm which of the three, if any, handled this basket, so P14 to any of them would assert exactly the fact the sources deny. This is the known cost of group attribution -- it does not tell you which members acted -- and the SIG has looked straight at it: in 2021 Robert Sanderson raised the 'workshop of / circle of' case, where 'not all members of the group did it, and the group is not necessarily "named", rather constructed', and asked for a subproperty of P14 meaning carried out by member or members of a group (t1477, Issue 542). It never arrived: the 57th meeting left the issue dependent on CRMsoc developments, and the register closes it at the 60th meeting (Bern, April 2025) because work on CRMsoc was discontinued. There is therefore no finer property to reach for; P14 to the group, with the caveat understood, is the current answer.

Why not a broader unspecified actor. E39 Actor's only declared subclasses are E21 Person and E74 Group; it means 'people, either individually or in groups' -- i.e. an agent of unknown kind. Instantiating E39 here throws away information you actually hold, namely that the agent was a collective. Uncertainty about *which individuals* is not a reason to climb the hierarchy, because it is not uncertainty about person-vs-group. Monotonicity also removes the motive for hedging: the group-level statement stays true if individuals are later established, so names can be added later without retracting anything.

Where the three names do go. Model the communal work session as its own E7 Activity and nest the basket's production in it with P9 consists of; then each named woman is an E21 Person attached to the *session* with P11 had participant (P14's superproperty, participation without the responsibility implication), and to the production with nothing at all. (The alternative is to treat the session itself as one collective E12 Production -- its scope note says 'This entity can be collective' -- with P108 has produced pinning each object; participation still has to stay at session level, so the E7 wrapper is the clearer of the two.) If the consultation also supports that these women belong to the household collective, add group P107 has current or former member person, optionally with P107.1 kind of member.

Because the three names come from a later community consultation rather than from the field record, wrap that identification as an E13 Attribute Assignment carried out by the consulting body: P140 assigned attribute to the session, P141 assigned the person, P177 assigned property of type a type standing for P11 had participant. E13's scope note is explicit that this construct marks the maintaining team as 'in general neutral to the validity of the respective assertion', registering someone else's opinion and how it came about -- exactly the status a name that cannot be tied to the object should have, and the practice recommended under Modelling principles > Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents. If a graded confidence is wanted rather than plain attribution, CRMinf's I2 Belief (with J4 that / J5 holds to be an I6 Belief Value) exists, at the cost of taking on an extension.

Two details on the edges of the question. The senior weaver may be recorded as an unnamed E21 Person carrying P14 on the production with P14.1 in the role of a 'senior weaver / supervising weaver' type -- the CRM's own P14 example is Michelangelo 'in the role of master craftsman' -- or, if asserting an unnamed individual is unwelcome, only as P107.1 kind of member within the collective. And the weaving cooperative the basket was collected from is a different E74 Group belonging on the collecting and custody side, not on P14 of the production; it should not be quietly promoted to maker because it is the better-documented body.

rejected_alternatives.option: E39 Actor as an unspecified agent
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E39 is the union of E21 Person and E74 Group -- 'people, either individually or in groups' -- so instantiating it says only that the kind of agent is unknown. The diary does tell us the agent was a collective, so E39 discards evidence. Monotonicity means the group-level assertion survives any later identification of individuals, so there is nothing to be gained by hedging upward.

rejected_alternatives.option: Three instances of E21 Person as the makers, via P14
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P14 carried out by 'implies causal or legal responsibility'; the consultation could not confirm which of the three, if any, handled this basket. Naming them on P14 asserts the one thing the sources rule out. They belong on P11 had participant on the work session instead.

rejected_alternatives.option: An E74 Group consisting of the three named women
rejected_alternatives.why_not: That invents a collective no source describes as acting as a unit, and it re-imports the same false claim at group level: the maker group would then be exactly those three, which the consultation does not support. The collective in the evidence is the household's women, whose full membership is not enumerated.

rejected_alternatives.option: E40 Legal Body for the household or the cooperative
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Deprecated; the migration table in the specification instructs to use E74 Group instead. No separate class is available or needed for a formally constituted cooperative.

rejected_alternatives.option: A subproperty of P14 meaning 'carried out by one or more members of the group'
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Requested for exactly this pattern in t1477 but never adopted. Issue 542 was left dependent on CRMsoc at the 57th meeting and closed at the 60th when CRMsoc work was discontinued, so no such property exists to cite.

siblings_considered.why_not: E21 Person is the other subclass of E39 Actor and is the rival the question puts forward. It is right for the three later-identified women and for the senior weaver as individuals, but wrong for the maker slot: the documented agent of this basket is a collective, and no individual can be tied to the object without asserting the responsibility P14 implies.

For the three named women, folding them into a group would erase what the consultation actually delivered -- three distinct, individually identified people -- and would silently constitute a collective that never acted as one. Individual identity is the whole point of these three records, so E21, attached only as participants.

E65 Creation covers conceptual and immaterial products. The coiled basket is a physical human-made thing, so its making is E12 Production (P108 has produced). E65 would only enter if one wanted to document the coiling design or pattern as a conceptual item, which the case does not ask about.

E63 Beginning of Existence is the class for events that bring a persistent item into existence; the communal work session is not defined by bringing this basket into being -- that part is the nested E12 Production, which is already both E11 Modification and E63. The session is wanted precisely as the wider intentional activity that the named women took part in.

E85 Joining is the sibling one would reach for to attach the three women to the household collective through documented membership events, and P107 is declared as a shortcut of the E85 path. But no joining events are documented, and what needs recording is not a membership event in the 1970s -- it is a present-day consultation making an assertion about the past, whose author and neutral status are what E13 Attribute Assignment exists to capture.

notes: Nothing in the corpus addresses ethnographic or communal making directly -- as expected, the model does not enumerate cases -- so the argument had to be built from the E74/E39 scope notes plus the one place the SIG attacked this exact boundary (t1477 / Issue 542), which ended without a solution when CRMsoc was discontinued. Two things the tools made awkward: (1) the group-level caveat is a real residual weakness of the recommendation, not something I can cite a resolution for -- the CRM simply has no way to say 'some members of this group, we do not know which' beyond P14 to the group; (2) `docs` prints no chunk ids, so declaration text cannot be quote-verified until you discover the id form (crm732#E74) via `docs ... --json`. Two `quote` calls failed first because I passed concept ids, which are not quotable sources. Lower confidence on one detail: whether to instantiate a separate E74 Group for 'the women of the household' as distinct from the household itself is a judgement call the sources do not settle; the household group alone, with P14.1 or P107.1 carrying the 'women / senior weaver' distinction, would also be defensible.
